text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn is expected to announce his party's nomination for the vacant post of welfare minister following a meeting of the Socialist Party presidium. Political State Secretary Mihaly Kokeny is hot favourite for the post.
- President Arpad Goncz Friday promoted police Col. Laszlo Forgacs to the rank of major general, coinciding with his appointment to head National Police Headquarters.
- Should all local governments suing the State Privatisation and Holding Co. emerge as winners, the holding will have to pay up some HUF 150 billion, said board chairman Arpad Kovacs.

- German banks appreciate the recent improvement in Hungary's finances and most will agree to lower the interest rate on the $350 million syndicated loan taken up by Hungary in August, outgoing vice president at the National Bank Frigyes Harshegyi said in Bonn.
- The American construction material manufacturing firm Butler is to establish its East European headquarters in Nyiregyhaza, according to an agreement signed Saturday.
- The far right Hungarian Justice and Life Party reelected incumbent Istvan Csurka as party president.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn pledged Sunday that real wages would not drop next year, while the rise in pensions would in fact exceed price increases.
- Karl Stix, prime minister of the Austrian Federal state Burgenland said Hungary's early membership of the European Union would present immeasurable dangers for the EU.
- Israeli Telecommunications Minister Limor Livnat will visit her Hungarian counterpart Karoly Lotz from December 17-19.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Parliament is set to ratify the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty this week, said Deputy Speaker of Parliament Maria Korodi. (Sat.)

- Ferenc Vegh, commander and chief of staff of the Hungarian Armed Forces, said after meeting Sir Jeremy MacKenzie, deputy commander in chief of NATO European Allied Forces in Budapest that Hungary is expected to continue its participation in the Bosnian peace efforts.
- Hungary's population has dropped by 340,000 since 1981.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- An internal survey of the opposition by the Socialist Party stresses the importance of making overtures toward the Young Democrats.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- A senior Interior Ministry official said the ministry is seeking to supervise the activities of the police more closely than in the past.
- Pannonhalma has been named world heritage site.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- An unnamed official of the Belgian company Tractabel has confirmed that the firm plans to sue the Hungarian state for damages and will seek to nullify the privatisation contract for a 48.7 percent stake in the power plant Dunamenti Eromu.
- No major boom is expected in the first half of next year in the processing and building industries, nor in retail trade, says a poll by Kopint-Datorg. (Sat.)
- This year's wage increases will exceed those of 1995 in every branch of the private sector, a study by Price Waterhouse says. (Sat.)
